title: 2 Chronicles 12
paragraphs: ¹ Once Rehoboam had secured the kingdom and established his power, he abandoned the law of the LORD — and all Israel followed him. ² In his fifth year, because they had been unfaithful to the LORD, Shishak king of Egypt attacked Jerusalem ³ with twelve hundred chariots, sixty thousand horsemen, and a countless army of Libyans, Sukkites, and Cushites from Egypt. ⁴ He captured the fortified cities of Judah and advanced all the way to Jerusalem. ⁵ Then the prophet Shemaiah came to Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah, who had gathered in Jerusalem to escape Shishak, and said to them, "This is what the LORD says: 'You have abandoned me, so I have abandoned you to Shishak.'"

⁶ The princes of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said, "The LORD is righteous." ⁷ When the LORD saw that they had humbled themselves, his word came to Shemaiah: "They have humbled themselves, so I will not destroy them. I will give them some relief, and my wrath will not be poured out on Jerusalem through Shishak. ⁸ But they will become his servants, so they will know the difference between serving me and serving the kings of other lands." ⁹ Shishak king of Egypt attacked Jerusalem and carried off the treasures of the temple of the LORD and the treasures of the royal palace. He took everything, including the gold shields Solomon had made. ¹⁰ King Rehoboam replaced them with bronze shields and assigned them to the commanders of the guard who watched over the palace entrance.

¹¹ Whenever the king entered the temple of the LORD, the guards came and carried the shields, and then returned them to the guardroom. ¹² Because Rehoboam humbled himself, the LORD's anger turned away from him, and he was not completely destroyed — things also went well in Judah. ¹³ King Rehoboam established himself firmly in Jerusalem and continued to reign. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel as the place to put his Name. His mother's name was Naamah; she was an Ammonite. ¹⁴ He did evil because he had not set his heart on seeking the LORD. ¹⁵ As for the events of Rehoboam's reign, from beginning to end, are they not written in the records of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer that deal with genealogies? There was continual warfare between Rehoboam and Jeroboam.
¹⁶ Rehoboam rested with his ancestors and was buried in the City of David. His son Abijah succeeded him as king.
